issue: Must a court consider a defendant's individual history and circumstances when deciding an as-applied Second Amendment challenge to 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(9) (and § 922(g)(1)), or may it apply a categorical, felony-by-felony test?

sides.position: Categorical, felony-by-felony approach: the court does not assess the defendant's individual history or characteristics in an as-applied challenge to the firearm prohibition.
cases: United States v. Kimble, 142 F.4th 308 (5th Cir. 2025)
United States v. Allred, No. 25-50204 (5th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: Individualized assessment: the court considers the defendant's history and conduct, or at least leaves that possibility open, in as-applied challenges to the firearm prohibition.
cases: United States v. Williams, 113 F.4th 637 (6th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Martin, No. 24-3750, 2025 WL 1913185 (6th Cir. July 11, 2025)
United States v. Simmons, 150 F.4th 126 (2d Cir. 2025)

this_court: Categorical, felony-by-felony approach (the majority follows Kimble and applies it to § 922(g)(9)); the individualized-assessment view appears only in Judge Graves's concurrence.
quote: "There is already a robust circuit split" regarding how courts should consider as-applied challenges to § 922(g)(1).
cite: United States v. Allred, No. 25-50204 (5th Cir. 2026)
